subject: general
question: Which of the following is **NOT **a component of the male reproductive part of flower?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **male reproductive organ **of a flower is called an **androecium**.
 
• It is made up of **stamens**.
 
• **Pollen grains **include **stamen**, which aids in the **development **of **male gametes**.
 
• In terminal sac-like structures called **anthers**, stamens produce pollen.
 
• The **anther **is made up of four **microsporangia**, which resembles the little sacs and **produce pollen for pollination.**
 
• Typically, stamens have a long, slender stalk, **filament**, and **anthers **at the terminal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **female reproductive system** of a flowering plant contains the component of style.
 
• It produces the **gynoecium**, or **pistil**, the female reproductive organ of the flower, along with the **stigma **and **ovary**.
 
• The **style **is the stalk that connects **stigma **with ovary.
 
• The **pollen grains arrive **at the **stigma **first during **pollination**, where they start to **germinate**.
 
• Under the direction of the secretions from the stigma, the pollen then forms a tube through the style called a pollen tube that ultimately travels to the **ovary**.
